A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sparse-attention study. Their complete main text, equations, 17 figures, Table 1 and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient-flow simulations and Transformer experiments on single-location linear regression and associative recall, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations, Transformer experiments and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The toy attention model, Transformer architectures, objectives and learning procedures are unchanged. Section 4 elaborates the existing active-learning conjecture with a prospective diversity schedule, without revising the specified methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic regression and associative-recall tasks, repetition conditions and task variants. The added discussion of arithmetic, factual associations and language introduces no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The theoretical-versus-simulation comparison and SGD-versus-Adam ablation retain the same comparators in Figures 9 and 15. The newly cited softmax-attention work is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The data-generation procedures, plateau thresholds, evaluation distributions, model configurations and learning-rate searches are unchanged, including the settings documented in Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: Both retain the same assumption-relaxation experiment, architecture/task/optimizer ablations, repetition-generalization analyses and attention-dynamics analysis in Appendices A–C. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains five seeds for Transformer regression and three for associative recall; Figure 9 still reports five simulation seeds. Statistical fitting and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All 17 figure graphics and their experimental findings are retained. Figure 4 still reports vocabulary and pair-count exponents of 0.79 and 2.25, with R2 = 0.982; Section 3.2 retains the fourfold and twofold repetition speedups.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, reduced dynamics and escape-time derivations remain unchanged, including Appendix A. The added explanations connect existing equations to their signal/noise interpretation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims about sparse-attention emergence, power-law timing and repetition benefits. The expanded discussion develops applications without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly states that the toy model cannot directly implement an induction head. Sections 2.3 and 4 expand the repetition interpretation, identify circumstances favoring each repetition type, and suggest lowering then raising data diversity during learning. These are qualifications and hypotheses, not new experimental findings.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same synthetic-data instructions, hyperparameters, software frameworks, RTX 3090 hardware, approximate training time and code-availability statement and URL.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Chen et al. (2024) on training dynamics of multi-head softmax attention, extending its connection to prior theory beyond linear Transformers. The remaining reference changes are relocation, renumbering or bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory rewrites, adds the 'When does repetition help?' discussion paragraph, expands the active-learning discussion and removes a duplicated citation. The overall section structure remains intact, and the publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 receive expanded captions explicitly linking the plots to theoretical predictions. Figure 5 moves from page 8 to page 9 as text reflows. Figure graphics and Table 1 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 improves conceptual precision by explicitly explaining the toy model's induction-head limitation, clarifying repetition mechanisms and acknowledging related softmax-attention theory. The application discussion is more informative but remains speculative. With the theory, experiments and reproducibility information unchanged, the overall gain is limited.
